title: How to get a virtual dollar card in Nigeria
summary: Looking for a virtual dollar card in Nigeria? Learn how to get one, compare your options, and create a Grey virtual Visa card for international payments.
body_markdown:
If you live in Nigeria and regularly pay for international services, you already know the problem. Naira cards come with monthly spending limits on international platforms. Some platforms do not accept them at all. Whether you are paying for subscriptions, buying software, or settling invoices with international clients, a naira card is often not enough.


A virtual dollar card solves this. It gives you a card funded in USD that works on global platforms, without needing a US bank account or a physical card. This guide explains what a virtual dollar card is, what to look for when choosing one, and exactly how to get and activate a Grey virtual dollar card in Nigeria.


## **What is a virtual dollar card?**


A[virtual dollar](https://grey.co/cards) **** card is a digital payment card linked to a US dollar balance. It has a card number, expiry date, and CVV, just like a physical card, but exists only in an app. You use it to make purchases online, pay for subscriptions, and transact with international merchants, without ever needing a physical piece of plastic.


The key difference from a naira card is what it is denominated in. When you pay on an international platform with a virtual dollar card, the transaction is processed in USD. There are no currency conversion issues at the point of payment, and there are no monthly international spending caps tied to your naira account.


## **Why Nigerians need a virtual dollar card**


Naira cards are useful for local transactions, but they have real limitations for international spending. The Central Bank of Nigeria sets monthly international spending limits on naira-denominated cards. These limits vary, but they can make it difficult or impossible to maintain consistent international subscriptions or pay for higher-cost services.


Beyond the limit issue, some international platforms have historically had friction in processing Naira card payments. A virtual dollar card removes this friction. Because the card is funded and processed in USD, the transaction looks and behaves like any other dollar payment to the merchant.


Common use cases for Nigerians with virtual dollar cards include:


- Paying for streaming services such as Netflix, Spotify, and YouTube Premium
- Buying software licenses and SaaS tools
- Paying for cloud storage, hosting, and developer platforms
- Subscribing to online courses and educational platforms
- Receiving and settling invoices on freelance platforms such as Upwork, Fiverr, and Toptal
- Shopping on international e-commerce platforms
- Paying for advertising on Meta, Google, and other international ad platforms

## **What to look for in a virtual dollar card**


Not all virtual dollar cards work the same way. Before you choose one, there are a few things worth comparing.


### **Card network**


Virtual dollar cards run on either Visa or Mastercard. Both are accepted on virtually all major international platforms. Visa has slightly broader acceptance on some US-based merchant platforms. Check which network your card runs on before you sign up, as a small number of platforms only accept one or the other.


### **Creation fee**


Some providers charge a one-time fee to create your virtual card. This is separate from any funding or top-up charges. Make sure you understand the full cost of getting the card before you commit. Some providers market cards as free, but charge for activation or funding.


### **FX and spending fees**


If you use your virtual dollar card to pay on a platform that processes in a currency other than USD, you will typically be charged a foreign exchange fee. This fee is usually a percentage of the transaction amount, sometimes with a fixed component. For USD-denominated platforms, this fee does not apply. Knowing this in advance lets you avoid it by choosing where to use each card.


### **Funding requirements**


Check the minimum balance required to activate and maintain the card. Some providers require you to hold a minimum USD balance before you can create a card. Factor this into your decision, along with the creation fee.


### **Supported platforms and restrictions**


Most virtual dollar cards work on the vast majority of international platforms. However, some providers place category restrictions on certain merchant types. If you have a specific platform in mind, confirm that the card is accepted there before signing up.


### **ATM withdrawal support**


Virtual cards are designed for online transactions. They do not support ATM withdrawals. If you need to withdraw cash, you will need a physical card from a different provider. This is a fundamental characteristic of virtual cards, not a limitation specific to any one provider.


## **How to get a Grey virtual dollar card in Nigeria: step by step**


Grey offers a[virtual Visa card](https://grey.co/cards) funded from your USD balance. Here is exactly how to get one.


### **Step 1: Download the Grey app and create your account**


Download the Grey app from the App Store or Google Play. Open the app and tap Create Account. Enter your email address and create a secure password. Grey is available to Nigerian residents.


### **Step 2: Complete identity verification**


Grey is a regulated platform and requires[identity verification](https://support.grey.co/en/articles/5249402-kyc-verification) before you can access full account features. You will need to provide your Bank Verification Number (BVN) and a valid government-issued ID, such as your national identity card, passport, or driver's license. Verification is completed in-app and typically takes a short time to process.


### **Step 3: Fund your USD wallet**


To create a virtual dollar card, you need at least $5 in your Grey USD wallet. You can fund your USD wallet by transferring from your naira account via your Grey account’s local USD funding options, or by receiving a USD transfer from another Grey user or an external USD account.


### **Step 4: Navigate to Cards in the app**


Once your USD wallet has at least $5, go to the Cards section of the Grey app. Tap Create Card and select a USD virtual card.


### **Step 5: Review and confirm the fees**


Before your card is created, Grey will show you the full cost upfront. The fees are:


- $4 one-time card creation fee
- $1 deducted from your USD balance as the initial card funding


Both charges are shown clearly before you confirm. You will not be surprised by hidden fees after the fact. Once you confirm, the fees are deducted, and your card is created.


### **Step 6: Start using your card immediately**


Your virtual card details are available immediately after creation. You will see your card number, expiry date, and CVV in the app. You can use these details right away to make purchases on any platform that accepts Visa payments.

## **What does a Grey virtual dollar card cost?**


Here is the full fee breakdown, so there are no surprises.


Fee type Amount


Card creation fee $4, charged once at the time of card creation


Initial funding deduction $1 deducted from your USD balance


Monthly fee None


Minimum USD balance required $5 before card creation


FX fee on non-USD transactions 2% of the transaction amount + $0.50, applied when a merchant processes your payment in a currency other than USD. Avoidable by using USD-denominated platforms.


***The FX fee applies only when you use your USD card on a platform that processes payments in another currency. For US-based platforms and services priced in USD, the fee does not apply. Most international subscriptions and SaaS platforms process in USD by default.***


## **What can you use a Grey virtual dollar card for?**


Your Grey virtual dollar card works on any platform that accepts Visa. Some of the most common uses include:


- International streaming services: Netflix, Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Premium
- Cloud platforms: AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure
- Developer and productivity tools: GitHub, Notion, Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud
- Advertising platforms: Meta Ads, Google Ads, TikTok Ads Manager
- E-commerce: Amazon, eBay, AliExpress, Etsy
- Freelance platform billing: Upwork, Fiverr, Toptal, Freelancer
- Online education: Coursera, Udemy, LinkedIn Learning
- Domain and hosting services: Namecheap, GoDaddy, Cloudflare, DigitalOcean


One thing to note: the Grey virtual card is for online payments only. It does not support ATM cash withdrawals. If you need physical cash in USD, you will need a separate arrangement.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **Is a Grey virtual dollar card free?**


No. Grey charges a $4 one-time fee to create your virtual card, plus a $1 deduction from your USD balance as the initial card funding. There is no monthly fee after that. You need at least $5 in your USD wallet before you can create the card.


### **Can I use a Grey virtual dollar card on Amazon Nigeria?**


Yes. Amazon accepts Visa cards, and the Grey virtual dollar card is a Visa card. When shopping on[Amazon.com](http://amazon.com/) or international storefronts, transactions are processed in USD, so no FX fee applies. For Amazon's local storefronts that price in other currencies, the 2% + $0.50 FX fee applies.


### **Can I use my virtual dollar card to withdraw from an ATM?**


No. Virtual cards are for online payments only. They do not have physical card details that can be read by an ATM, and they are not linked to a physical card. If you need to withdraw cash, you will need a separate physical card.


### **Is Grey available in Nigeria?**


Yes. Grey is fully available in Nigeria. You can download the app, create an account, complete identity verification using your BVN and a valid Nigerian ID, and start using your multi-currency account, including your virtual dollar card.


### **What is the spending limit on a Grey virtual dollar card?**


Grey sets spending limits based on account verification level and card usage. Check the Grey app or Grey's support center for current limits. Unlike naira cards, there is no CBN-imposed monthly international spending cap on your Grey USD card.


### **What happens if my card details are compromised?**


Because Grey's card is virtual, your card details exist only in the app. You can delete a compromised card and create a new one through the app. Your underlying USD balance is separate from the card details and is not affected.


## **Common mistakes to avoid with your virtual dollar card**


Getting the card is the easy part. The following mistakes are the ones that cost people money or cause transactions to be declined.


### **Using your USD card on sterling or naira-priced platforms**


If you use your Grey USD card to pay on a platform that prices in GBP or NGN, the 2% + $0.50 FX fee applies. This is avoidable. For Nigerian platforms priced in naira, use a naira payment method. For UK-priced services, use your GBP wallet and a GBP card if you have one. Reserve your USD card for USD-denominated platforms, where it performs best with no FX costs.


### **Not having enough balance for both the creation fee and the first payment**


The card creation fee deducts $4, and the initial funding fee deducts $1, totaling $5 from your USD wallet. If you fund exactly $5 and create the card, your available balance after creation is $0. You need to fund above $5 before creating the card if you want to make a payment immediately after.


### **Entering card details on unfamiliar sites**


Your Grey virtual card details are as sensitive as any other card details. Only enter them on platforms you trust. If a site looks unfamiliar or asks for your card number via email or chat, do not use it. Grey cannot reverse transactions made to fraudulent merchants. If you are unsure about a platform, create a separate virtual card with a small balance specifically for that transaction.


### **Expecting the card to work at ATMs**


This is the most common point of confusion. Virtual cards have no magnetic strip, no chip, and no physical presence. They cannot be inserted into or tapped at ATMs. If you need cash while abroad or locally, you will need a physical card from a separate provider.


### **Forgetting to check the merchant's processing currency**


Some international platforms process in local currency even if they are priced in USD. For example, a platform based in the EU may display prices in USD but process your card in EUR. In that case, the FX fee applies even though the price is shown in dollars. If a platform processes in USD, there is no fee. When in doubt, check the platform's billing terms or test with a small charge first.


## **How to fund your Grey USD wallet**


Before you can create or top up your virtual dollar card, you need USD in your Grey wallet. There are several ways to do this.


- **Convert from your naira balance:** If you have NGN in your Grey account, you can convert it to USD in-app at Grey's published exchange rate. A 1% conversion fee applies.
- **Receive a USD transfer:** If someone sends you USD to your[Grey USD account](https://grey.co/foreign-accounts) using your ACH routing number and account number, it arrives directly in your USD wallet with no conversion needed.
- **Convert from GBP or EUR:** If you hold GBP or EUR in Grey, you can convert those to USD in-app. The 1% conversion fee applies.
- **Receive USDC:** Grey supports the[USDC stablecoin](https://grey.co/usdc) . If you receive USDC into your Grey account, you can convert it to USD to fund your card.


Exchange rates are variable and are shown to you before you confirm any conversion. Always check the rate at the time of conversion rather than assuming a fixed rate.
